verdict.rationale: Antigravity's docs say Projects give agents 'all of the context required for your codebase', and the agent can delegate 'extensive codebase searches' to built-in subagents, so it can explore a repo autonomously without the user picking context files. Artifacts can include architecture diagrams, which supports explaining a codebase. However, no evidence explicitly documents an end-to-end 'map and explain the whole unfamiliar codebase' workflow, and there is no hands-on corroboration. Missing for 10: explicit documented codebase-mapping/explanation feature, evidence of automatic repo indexing or whole-codebase understanding at scale, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent map and explain an entire unfamiliar codebase without manually selecting context files

citations.quote: providing your agents with all of the context required for your codebase
an agent can delegate tasks—such as running tests or performing extensive codebase searches—to dedicated subagents.
Artifacts include rich markdown plans (Implementation Plans), code diffs, architecture diagrams, images, and browser recordings.
Build AI agents that autonomously read files, run commands, edit code, and more.
